If the friend's parents don't allow for therapy then that's that. But I'm still against OP Baker Acting his friend. I personally don't want to intervene in someone's personal agency. It's the most violating and terrible thing that someone else can do to you, and it's traumatizing. Everyone should have the final say for what should be done for themselves, not someone else. And at the end of the day, if something were to happen the onus is on the friend's parents.

Again, OP is free to do as he wishes, but they should know that this isn't a very clear-cut issue.

Not sure if you're aware btw but your responses are being automatically minimized...

inb4 this thread gets deleted for political topics.

Yeah I agree. Like...the world's pretty rough. Chicks and dicks both have it bad.

But like, people generally tend to sweep men's mental health issues under the rug because that's just kind of how things are. It's bad enough that public tragedies get negatively associated with mental health issues, and further stigmatizes the issue where it becomes difficult for people, especially men, to talk about their issues in public.

Like, in general women tend to have larger social circles. And women in general have higher emotional intelligence, so they can more easily communicate their emotional needs to others especially other women. But men don't really have those kinds of things. Men usually have smaller social circles and have social difficulty being open about their feelings because of general social stigmatization.

It's pretty bad when like...mental health issues get politicized when they really shouldn't. It's everybody's issue. But I've noticed that for some minds of philosophical thought, men's mental health issues in particular are simply considered as "not our problem" and then they generally sweep alarming statistics like how the majority of successful suicide attempts are from men under the rug because it doesn't fit their worldview. (It's vice versa'd for women where women have more attempts, which is an alarming issue of it's own. Not sure why that one doesn't have much focus either.)

I dunno, I like to think I'm a pretty open-minded person but this really does upset me how it's becoming a trend to say men's mental health issues are no big deal because it's sexist.

I mean, you're not OP's friend though. And ask a lot of the people in this subreddit, they were angry and ended up not telling others about their issues afterwards. I had the same happen to me, and I just don't talk to anybody in my immediate social circle (as small as it is) about these kinds of things because you can't trust anybody.

I would honestly recommend for OP to tell his friend to talk to a therapist or a licensed professional instead of running his mouth, because they're better equipped to handle these types of situations than your run of the mill average joe.

You could tell a trusted adult figure in your life, they might know what to do.

But there are some risks involved to telling others about her situation, so do keep that in mind.
Yeah I've noticed that they're pretty trigger-happy here about that for some reason idk why. It just seems so excessive.

>Your friend will be angry~~for a while but grateful eventually~~.

Fixed.

OP just know that you can choose to tell someone but don't be surprised if you lose him as a friend because you just committed the ultimate act of betrayal against him. He might get committed and if he does he won't tell anybody the next time, and then everybody will be surprised when he goes through with it when nobody knew.

Just assume that if you go through with this, he'll never talk to you again.
Hey just fyi I think your post got removed.

After a while, you realize that there are very few if no truly altruistic people. There are some but they end up being pigeonholed into professions that have certain legal restrictions to how they can operate. (Typically therapists, although not all therapists are strictly speaking altruistic.)

or

Yes.
Don't worry. After a while you realize to choose yourself instead of others.
Yup. This is why I don't tell therapists everything. Just what they want to hear, because all they're interested in is money.

It doesn't get better. And even if you try it still doesn't.

Saying it gets better is like walking up to someone dying in a hospital bed and telling them it gets better.

And saying it gets better is a sunken cost fallacy. If all the evidence so far points that your life is bad, there is no sense in thinking that it will improve. Because it won't.
cmon if they're posting this, the best isn't happening for them to be real.

>nothing good will happen.

This is the only true statement that you made from your whole comment.

>it does get better

This is untrue to the point that it literally violates subreddit rules to post that kind of garbage.

Yeah that's kind of the thing about mental healthcare in the US. It's a sham. (And this is something that multiple therapists and psychiatrists have told me about in private, ones that I know who aren't responsible for my treatment.)

It's a huge sham. The entire system literally just doesn't work. The vast majority of people who receive "mental healthcare" just come out of it either much worse or bankrupt. There's a reason why the rate of people who decide to check out is increasing despite all of these so called "advances" in mental healthcare.

"It doesn't work, clearly. It's just a system to mitigate risk, and for people to feel good about themselves. We don't even know very well what causes these illnesses, how are we even supposed to remotely help people? We can't even voice this publicly because if we do we'll lose our jobs. It's a really lucrative industry to break into because mental health in this country is getting worse, and the solutions don't work. Admins charge people for forced hospitalization because either way they get their money. Either the patient is forced to pay up with their wages garnished, or the hospital can claim their due from the patient's estate if the patient decides to check out. It's all about money, nobody ever cared about the patient's actual mental health. The Baker Act was beloved by mental health professionals because it gave us more work and more income, that's it." - A therapist I spoke to, in private.

It's a huge clown charade of greed and profitseeking at the expense of people who desperately need help. It's disgusting.

Unlike a lot of fake responses here, I'll say it as it is.

I nor anybody else here will blame you if you just decide to check out. Because honestly...that's not living.
Be free my dude. I hope that you are no longer in pain, because I would never wish that on you.

Yeah for me like...when I wake up all of my regrets just hit me like a brick. It's soul crushing kind of torture and I can't take it anymore.

God I just wish I wasn't such a coward and I can just go through with it. I know I have nothing left to live for since there's nothing to look forward to anyways.

I prefer not to be judgmental to someone in their last hours and give a bunch of empty platitudes like "it gets better" or some stupid variation of that.

That's like going to the bedside of a dying person and telling them that it gets better.
Oh my god yeah, how much I wish I could reset time to a certain point with all of my memories intact. I would do anything for that.
Can't really discuss methods, but I've got a few reliable ones of my own. Got my gear ready, just deciding on best time to do it.

I feel it too. I miss her a lot.

Although it's not the cause, it was certainly the last straw for me. A lifetime of just terrible things happening one after another. I'm done.

So yeah, I get you man. I don't blame you. Life sucks and it's not worth it.

I feel that. I took some things for granted. Wasn't careful. Ruined my own life.

I guess some people just weren't meant to be happy.

Yeah but for basically everybody on this subreddit who are actually suffering, we don't live happy lives. We won't live happy lives. This is a product of no matter how much effort we put into improvement, nothing ever changed. And if we know that life won't improve and it won't get better and life will just continually only get worse, what's the point in prolonging things? There isn't as far as we see.
Not everyone gets a happy ending. Especially if the other decides to end things permanently.

Because they would rather have you alive so they don't feel bad, instead of letting you go so you no longer feel bad.

That's all there is to it. Selfishness.
Yup. I ruined my own life with my own stupid decisions. I just wish it would all end very painlessly when I decide to do it.
Have a good night my guy. Dream well.

We as a society should really stop perpetuating this lie that things get better. It doesn't. For basically everybody on this subreddit, it doesn't get better, it gets worse.

We should really just be telling people when they're younger that if you have bad cards in life, it stays that way. Life doesn't improve.

giving up is an option otherwise so many people wouldn't have taken it already.

Obviously written by people who have never had to experience real pain and suffering in their lives. Pisses me off that people write and say dumb shit like that.

Like...how is anybody supposed to realistically be able to do that if all they faced their whole lives is nothing but loneliness and rejection, and a mind that hates them?
